item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-12 15:00
Institution: Politecnico TORINO, Torino
Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/IEGE-01 Ingegneria economico-gestionale

The project examines how to assess and guide the social impact of innovation in organisations and mobility systems. It combines two research areas: workplace diversity and inclusion strategies, focusing on equal opportunities, participation and organisational well-being; and the adoption of smart electric mobility solutions, considering socioeconomic benefits, industrial effects and sustainability. A shared framework of indicators and evaluation methods will measure how outcomes differ across people, organisations and places, and identify the conditions and practices that make technological transitions more equitable and effective.

Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/IIND-06 Macchine e sistemi per l'energia e l'ambiente

Heating and cooling of buildings account for a predominant share of energy consumption and CO2 emissions. The challenge of the energy transition and decarbonization of this sector involves citizens, operators, municipalities and policymakers, each with different roles and prerogatives. An integrated approach is needed, which finds concrete application in the Local Heating and Cooling Plan (LHCP) provided for by Directive (EU) 2023/1791 on energy efficiency (EED). Building the databases and the evolution scenarios of an LHCP requires dedicated tools.

item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-13 15:00
Institution: Politecnico TORINO, Torino
Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/IIND-01 Ingegneria aerospaziale e navale

Limited understanding of how acoustic waves interact with turbulent boundary layers over sound-absorbing surfaces leads to unexpected, unphysical results in inverse acoustic characterization. This project will combine experiments with high-fidelity lattice-Boltzmann very-largeeddy simulations to explain flow–acoustic interactions. Advanced data analysis will separate acoustic and hydrodynamic velocities near the wall. The numerical database will enable comparison of inverse methods, reveal the physical causes of anomalous results and support physicsbased corrections. It will also help model and predict the drag increase caused by acoustic–flow coupling. These findings will resolve…
